name: checkpoint-snapshot-on-first-write
description: The checkpoint net arms itself. Nobody asked for a snapshot and nothing was committed first, yet by the time the agent's first `create` has run there is a freecode-snapshot commit in the shadow repo under $FREECODE_HOME/snapshots/ — taken lazily at the first write, so a read-only turn would have cost nothing. The second tool call reads the shadow repo back out through the real git binary, which is what makes this an end-to-end check rather than a mock: the ref, the commit, and its message all have to exist on disk. It blanks FREECODE_SNAPSHOT_DIR so its snapshots land under its own $FREECODE_HOME rather than the suite-wide directory, where the lookup would find every other scenario's shadow repo too. That lookup runs through `node -e` rather than shell syntax because `shell_exec` runs under cmd.exe on Windows, where `$VAR` and `*` glob expansion do not exist
